Two subjects in origami are badly served by the printed page: folding from crease patterns, and rigid origami. A crease pattern wants to be zoomed, printed at the size of your paper, and watched as it folds. Rigid origami is about motion. Both are natural subjects for a web book, and that is what I plan to write here, chapter by chapter, in the open.

Along the way: notes on the mathematics, reviews of the books I read, and the occasional origami-inspired object that is worth knowing about.
